title: Residual Calibration via Local Feature-Space Refinement
claim: Even when learned representations cleanly separate training data, held-out calibration samples stay mixed near class boundaries, so calibration support is uneven.
layout: 2 panels side by side, left-to-right, dashed circle with callout annotation
description: Two scatter plots sit side by side. Panel (a), 'Raw feature space', shows two overlapping Gaussian-like clouds in blue and orange. Filled circles are training points and faint crosses are calibration points, and they intermingle broadly. Panel (b), 'Learned feature space', shows a curved, elongated manifold. Blue training points form a clean arc on the left and orange points form a dense arc on the right. Faint calibration crosses of both classes scatter around the junction between the arcs. A dashed green circle marks a neighborhood near the boundary. A green line connects it to a callout: 'local calibration frequency=0.50, true probability=0.45'. Each panel has a legend for train classes versus calibration set. Blue and orange mark the two classes. The eye goes first to the dashed circle in (b).
caption: Representation separation can not guarantee uniform calibration support. (a) Raw features of training and calibration samples. (b) Learned features separate the training samples clearly, but calibration samples can remain mixed near induced boundary regions. Different colors represent different classes. The highlighted neighborhood illustrates the local evidence used by LAPE.
abstract: Deep neural networks often struggle to provide reliable confidence estimates, making post-hoc calibration essential for reliable decision-making. Existing post-hoc methods largely rely on score-based transformations, which improve marginal calibration but often fail to capture spatially varying miscalibration in local regions of the learned feature space. To address this gap, we propose Local Adaptive Probability Estimation (LAPE), a post-hoc residual calibration framework. Specifically, LAPE treats the global calibrator output as a stable anchor and refines the individual prediction by leveraging non-parametric local evidence from neighboring calibration samples. As a plug-and-play refinement module, LAPE effectively utilizes the information about feature-space geometry and can reuse the calibration data that are used to construct the global calibrator. Furthermore, we extend LAPE to the setting with multi-view inputs through Cascade Feature Augmentation Fusion (CFAF). Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed methods can improve the calibration quality of various existing baselines and remain efficient and robust across different settings.
